base_member_text: [L8-L13,L23-L26] (MED/C interoperability) POSIX usleep is declared as a void subroutine with a signed c_int argument even though the C function returns int and takes useconds_t, leaving the binding nonconforming and allowing negative or overflowing delays.
audit_member_text: [L9-L12] (MED/foreign-interface mismatch) The POSIX usleep routine is declared as a C-interoperable subroutine even though the C API returns an integer status, so the binding does not match the external function's prototype.

base_member_text: [L43-L52] (LOW/portability / timing semantics) The fallback calls a nonstandard sleep routine after truncating microseconds to whole seconds, so unsupported compilers silently lose subsecond throttling and depend on an undeclared platform-specific interface.

audit_member_text: [L23-L25,L28-L33,L36-L41,L44-L51] (LOW/input-contract inconsistency) myusleep does not reject negative durations and applies backend-dependent coercion, while the Intel/PGI paths also force zero or sub-millisecond requests to sleep at least one millisecond.
